title: fix(providers): the ObjectStack upload adapter never sends an upload path as the storage scope (objectui#12055)
body:
Part of #12055
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

## Summary

`createObjectStackUploadAdapter` sent `scope: opts.scope ?? options.path` at two sites: the presigned upload request body and `UploadResult.meta`. An adapter built without a `scope` therefore turned an upload's generic `path` into the storage scope. That `path` is a key prefix for the S3 and Azure presign callbacks, and the server refuses any scope that is not a value of its `sys_file` scope select.

This PR lands the half of objectui#12055 that every reading of the card shares:

- Both sites read only the adapter's own `scope`. With none, the request carries no `scope` and the server applies its default.
- The `scope` docblock drops the key-prefix examples ("avatars", "logos", "attachments/case") and names the server's `sys_file` scope select as the vocabulary. The `UploadOptions.path` docblock says the ObjectStack adapter never sends it.
- New pins in `packages/providers/src/__tests__/objectstack-upload-scope-12055.test.ts` cover the path case, the forwarding case and the two upload shapes this repo uses.
- `.changeset/12055-upload-path-not-scope.md`: `@object-ui/providers` minor, with the breaking meaning and the remedy stated.

The option's type is unchanged (`string`). The card's type half is not in this PR: typing `scope` from `@objectstack/spec`'s `StorageScope`, and the type-level pin that refuses `scope: 'avatars'`. Measurement falsified its premise (next section), so the card stays open for that decision. The first line is `Part of`, not a closing keyword, because the card goes to the decision box.

## Why the type half stops: `StorageScope` is not the upload vocabulary

Measured at the `@objectstack/spec` version objectui installs (17.7.0, the lockfile's resolution):

- `StorageScope` is exported from `@objectstack/spec/system` as the `z.input` of `StorageScopeSchema`. It has ten members: global, tenant, user, session, temp, cache, data, logs, config, public. `public` is still in it.
- The server's upload vocabulary is a different list. It is the `scope` select on the `sys_file` object in `@objectstack/service-storage`: user, tenant, public, private, temp, attachments. The two upload-starting handlers pass the caller's value straight to that insert. objectstack-ai/objectstack#22443's dev report (`6079733604`) measured the same split: `StorageScopeSchema` is read only by `ObjectStorageConfigSchema.scope`.
- The spec's upload request schema, `GetPresignedUrlRequestSchema`, declares `scope` as an open `z.string()` with default `user`.
- A compile probe typed against `StorageScope` refuses `'private'` and `'attachments'` (TS2322) and accepts `'global'`.

So typing the option as `StorageScope` would stop `RecordAttachmentsPanel` (`scope: 'attachments'`) from compiling. It would also refuse a value the server accepts (`private`) and admit six that the server refuses (global, session, cache, data, logs, config). The claim keeps `RecordAttachmentsPanel` and `@objectstack/spec` off the file surface, so I stopped there. The options are in the dev report on the card.

## Hypotheses

- **H1, falsified in its operative part.** The export exists: `StorageScope` and `StorageScopeSchema` from `@objectstack/spec/system`, ten members, `public` included. It is not the server's upload vocabulary (above).
- **H2, holds for the server's vocabulary but not for `StorageScope`.** Callers of `createObjectStackUploadAdapter`: the console's app-wide adapter (`apps/console/src/App.tsx`, no `scope`) and `RecordAttachmentsPanel` (`scope: 'attachments'`). Two suites mock the factory: `App.uploadAltitude-10131` and `RecordAttachmentsPanel.affordanceGrant-12047`. Upload calls: `ProfilePage` `upload(file)`, the organization `SettingsPage` `upload(file)`, `AvatarField` `upload(file)`, `FileField` `upload(file, { onProgress })`, `ImageField` `upload(blob)` and `upload(file)`, and `RecordAttachmentsPanel` `adapter.upload(file)`. None passes a `path`. Nothing reads `UploadResult.meta.scope`. `'attachments'` is in the server's vocabulary and not in `StorageScope`.
- **H3, holds and is pinned.** The two in-repo shapes send the same presign body on `main` and on this head, measured by the reverse leg below. With no scope and no path, the body is `filename`, `mimeType` and `size`. With `scope: 'attachments'` and no path, it also carries `scope: 'attachments'`.
- **H4, neutral.** `@object-ui/providers` is eager in the console (`App.tsx` imports it at module scope). I ran `vite build` of `apps/console` under the verify lock twice, at this head and with `main`'s blob of the adapter. The chunk that carries the adapter (`ui-components-*`) measured 1098012 bytes raw and 282728 gzip on `main`, and 1097996 raw and 282729 gzip on head: 16 bytes smaller raw, 1 byte larger gzip. Both builds emitted 2474 JS chunks. The budget bot's CI reading is still to come.

## Tests and gates (head `d28934975`, every run after the last commit)

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/providers/ apps/console/src/__tests__/App.uploadAltitude-10131.test.tsx packages/app-shell/src/views/__tests__/RecordAttachmentsPanel.affordanceGrant-12047.test.tsx packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/column-identity.ratchet.test.ts scripts/__tests__/one-authority-per-exported-name-6273.test.ts`, run from the repo root under the lock: `Test Files 7 passed (7)`, `Tests 39 passed (39)`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`. That covers every `packages/providers` suite, both suites that mount the adapter factory, and both repo-wide ratchets.
- `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/providers^...' build` (the closure, `@object-ui/types`), then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/providers type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): `VERDICT command-exit 0`. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists the new test file, so the test program compiles it.
- Callers' type-check (`@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/console`): not run locally, and owed to CI. The published declaration is unchanged. I emitted declarations with `--removeComments` for this head and for `main`'s blob, and `UploadProvider.d.ts` is byte-identical (1995 bytes). No caller's compile can move.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `check-changeset-fixed.mjs`, `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs`, `check-changeset-claims.mjs` and `check-pending-changeset-literals.mjs`: all exit 0.
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)`, exit 0. `check:control-bytes`, `check-test-path-roots` and `check-vi-mock-specifiers` also exit 0.
- `check:phantom-deps` and `docs:check-links` are not owed: no `package.json` and no docs page changed.
- ESLint, narrowed to the files this diff touches: `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config --format json` on the two `.ts`/`.tsx` files returned 2 results, 0 errors and 7 warnings, all in `UploadProvider.tsx` (`react-refresh/only-export-components` and `react-hooks/refs`, on code this diff does not touch). `main`'s blob of that file gives the same 0 errors and 7 warnings. The population is `eslint.config.js`'s own `**/*.{ts,tsx}` glob. That config enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions` or `projectService`), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.
- Governed-surface guard: `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on the three paths answered `NOT GOVERNED`.

## Reverse leg

The fix was committed first (`d28934975`). `main`'s blob of `packages/providers/src/UploadProvider.tsx` was written to disk, and its hash was checked against `main`'s blob. The anchor `opts.scope ?? options.path` counted 2 on disk. On that blob the new file ran `Tests 1 failed | 3 passed (4)`. The failure was the path pin (`expected true to be false`: the body carried `scope`). The forwarding pin and both in-repo shape pins stayed green, which is H3's evidence. A trap restored the file with `git checkout HEAD --`. The restore was proven by the on-disk hash matching `HEAD`'s blob, by an empty `git diff HEAD`, and by an anchor count of 0. On head the file runs `4 passed`. No type-level pin is in this PR (see above).

## Acceptance notes

- **Docs.** No docs page documents the adapter's options. `content/docs/fields/file.mdx` names `createObjectStackUploadAdapter` but documents neither `scope` nor `path`. `packages/providers/README.md` does not cover the upload provider. The option docblocks are the documentation, and this PR rewrites them.
- **Unchanged.** `RecordAttachmentsPanel`, `apps/console/src/App.tsx`, `packages/providers/package.json`, the lockfile, `@objectstack/spec` and every `packages/i18n` key are unchanged. Nothing is exported from any package.
- **Noted, not filed.** The spec's `StorageScope` is named like the upload scope but holds an unrelated vocabulary, and that is how this card's premise formed. Whether the spec declares the upload vocabulary (an enum for `GetPresignedUrlRequestSchema.scope`) is the open triage question on objectstack-ai/objectstack#22470, which owns it.

## Review

This landing owes the `domain:ui#2` seat's contract-tier review of record on this PR, per the claim on the card.
